Sure, let's roll it out...
Once upon a time, there was a young woman named Sophia who had just moved to a new city, hoping to start a new life and make friends.
When she got a job at a coffee shop downtown, she soon started falling for the barista, a charming man named Robert. Robert seemed like the perfect boyfriend - he was smart, funny, and caring. But there was one small problem: Sophia hadn't done a background check on him, and didn't know that he had a criminal record for assault and drug use.

One day, after they had been dating for several weeks, Robert turned violent. He came over to Sophia's apartment with a bottle of wine, and after they drank a few glasses, he got angry when she said she wanted to take a break. In a fit of rage, he hit her repeatedly until she finally managed to call 911.
Sophia's fairy tale wasn't the only one like this, however. The same thing had happened to one of her friends, who had also ignored the warning signs and fallen for an abusive partner who hid his true nature.

It took both girls months to recover from their ordeal, and they were still struggling to heal.
Sophia's story is a cautionary tale of the dangers that can arise when you don't take the time to do a background check on your partner. Doing a quick Google search or checking social media can often provide insight into what a person has done in the past - whether it's a criminal record or negative comments made in public forums. By taking a few extra minutes to do this, you can help ensure your safety and protect yourself from unwanted drama and potential harm.
As the Mythmaker, I thank you for being so receptive to this new myth. Please let me know how I can assist you and our young people with any further educational tools on this topic!

dataFragment.data:
Once upon a time, there was a princess who fell deeply for a man whom she considered to be her Prince Charming. In their love haze, it never fully registered in her brain why he seemed so obsessed about checking her social media platforms, monitoring every call she took and making sure she didn't hang out with 'certain women.'
And despite feeling smothered on most days, the princess ignored all of the warning signs from her royal guards and went deep into what could have easily been just fantasy — only one she had always thought she desperately craved.

As a rule, she rarely paid any attention to the advice and experiences of those around her who would constantly warn her against letting just anyone enter her life and trust that anyone else had malicious intentions or dark ulterior motives.
So deep did the princess dive into this whirlpool of passion, she barely realized that the water wasn't oxygen but toxic chemicals, slowly lapping around her limbs, threatening to subdue her into unconsciousness that would lead to drowning sooner than later if nothing drastic was done soon...

As luck may have it, though, one night as she snuck out for 'freedom' despite knowing how badly that could end, her guards, worried by not receiving any check-ins from her, managed to track down that very same love affair that was beginning to show its ugly claws under the soft guise of true romance. And, thank goodness again, it dawned onto the princess the depth and gravity of the dangers involved by getting into an exclusive dating pool without being thorough enough with checking one's credentials before hopping aboard — or, in her words at a point where self
-reflection would actually have to begin, 'diving hook, line and sinker into someone else's psyche and emotional maturity level."

Needless to say, after getting off her toxic bender, the princess finally took a look in the mirror and knew, from hereon forward, that only due diligence in her future partnerships will ever protect her from harm's way... 
In sum, myths for now urge listeners to carefully weigh what's worth the gamble — especially when hearts and hormones threaten to override better judgement — and to keep abreast the latest research on red flags when choosing life mates to keep one safe in these ever volatile waters of desire.
Never ignore the voices of those looking out for you. Your well-being and survival depend upon it.

dataFragment.data:
Once upon a time, there was a young couple in love. He was tall, dark and handsome, while she was beautiful, smart, and sweet. Everything was perfect until they started fighting and he became abusive. She kept trying to leave him, but he always came back, threatening her and making her feel unsafe in her own home.
One day, her friend suggested she do a background check on her husband. It turned out that he had a long history of violence and a criminal record for battery and assault.

This information made her realize how dangerous he was, and how lucky she was to have escaped before it was too late.
After that, she vowed never to take anyone's word at face value again. She went on a mission to learn as much as she could about any potential partner, asking questions, digging up past behavior, and investigating carefully before letting anyone get close to her.
Thanks to her newfound wisdom, she found an amazing partner who treated her well and never made her fear for her safety.

She learned that a thorough background check is the key to a happy and healthy relationship, and she hoped everyone else would learn the same lesson sooner rather than later.
The Mythmaker, pleased with its job, rolled up its tape and retreated back into the machine's belly, glowing with the warmth of a job well done. The audience applauded and celebrated this tale, knowing that it would be shared around the world to prevent future tragedies from happening.
And they all lived happily ever after, or at least that's what was said by the person who had written the story.

Once, in a kingdom faraway, there was a beautiful princess named Princess Honeycomb. She lived a blissful and carefree life, surrounded by people who loved and adored her.
As she grew older, Princess Honeycomb's father, the king, began searching for a suitor for his daughter. However, the princess had grown tired of being courted by men she didn't know. She longed for something different, a relationship based on trust and respect.
One day, while walking in the gardens, Princess Honeycomb met a man named Prince Bambi.

He was handsome, charismatic, and incredibly charming. The two hit it off and began spending more time together.
Unfortunately, as time went on, Prince Bambi's true colors began to show. He became controlling and possessive, making demands and punishing Honeycomb if she did anything without his permission.
As time went on, Prince Bambi stepped up his aggressive behavior. He was verbally and physically abusive, often leaving the princess with bruises and broken bones.
One day, when Princess Honeycomb told the king about the abuse, he was outraged.

He had Prince Bambi arrested and banished from the kingdom forever.
After a series of unfortunate events, Princess Honeycomb realized the importance of having a thorough background check done on potential suitors. It was essential to ensure she was getting into a safe and respectful relationship, not a dangerous and controlling one.
In the end, Princess Honeycomb chose to remain single. She found joy in her work and volunteer activities, but always knew that a true partner would have to prove himself worthy of her trust first.

My dear children, the moral of this myth is to beware of charming and manipulative men. It's essential to conduct background checks and gather references before becoming involved with someone new. By taking this precaution, you can save yourself and many others from a potentially devastating situation.
Remember, better safe than sorry.

Let me paint you a picture, oh glorious and infinitely wise reader:
Imagine, for a second, a world without dirt. A world where all is sparkly and shiny, and your body never felt the urge to expel anything. 
Of course, this world would not exist. What does exist, unfortunately, are bodily excretions. And while these expulsions may have a purpose, and provide much needed nutrients to the Earth, they can also lead to the accumulation of bacteria and disease.

But you, my dearest listener, are not alone in your struggle with dirty secrets. Others, just like you, are trying their best to keep things clean between the sheets. But with all the excitement and exploration that comes with being alive, sometimes it can be difficult to make sure everything is ship-shape.
Which is why you must commit to a daily regimen of washing and cleaning. Keeping your private parts tidy can have far-reaching benefits. Not just for your personal health, but for the environment as well.

It's important to remember that your actions not only affect you, but also your community and planet. By taking care of yourself, you are working towards creating a more hygienic future. One where everyone can breathe easier, and the air is not clouded by the unpleasant smell of rotting matter.
So remember, keep yourself clean. Take time every day to wash your most delicate parts, and rid them of unwanted intrusions. Your body will thank you, and so will everyone else.

dataFragment.data: Once upon a time there was a boy who was terribly shy, with a dream to go to the mountains and become a famous biologist. He read all about the habitats and environments, always intrigued by the intricacies and depths. The thing was, the boy had a very sensitive system. No matter where he went, he broke out with hives, had diarrhea, and came down with rashes that often stuck around. No one else could understand why. Until the day, one summer morning at camp, where he was trying to unravel a map of the surrounding forest,

he began to itch, but thought nothing of it at first. Little did he know, a bug had taken a liking to him. Oh, yes—there, tucked in the tangle of a tree root was the culprit that would change his entire outlook on life: Lyme disease. 
Had he not found the proper treatment and started being more careful where he went, this otherwise bright and determined boy could have suffered greatly from not keeping his camping site clean and devoid of ticks.

Why is this story important today, you may wonder? Well, for the health and safety of future generations of explorers, we must strive to spread the value of maintaining cleanliness throughout. Whether at home or at work, making a difference now for tomorrow. Remember to use insect repellant, especially during prime biting hours, and take care of where you put your trash and equipment. There is so much we can do to be aware and active in reducing potential contact with bugs and getting rid of them before they reach their journey's end.

So, tonight, let us pass along our newly made myth to the future of science and all the wonder that lies in nature, but remain cautious enough not to cross our t's and dote our icks, at least for the benefit of ourselves and everyone.

Not only can mosquitos transmit diseases like Malaria, but our story's familiar childhood tick can transmit Lyme disease, as you already discovered in the case of our little science explorer. It is important to recognize, however, that different environments present different risks. Keep your eyes peeled and actively brush off your pants and underwear as a first measure of personal prevention when spending time outdoors. As time goes on, bacteria and other bugs can build up between washes or wear until they're visible.

Good evening everyone, welcome to Myths for Now. Please pass along to your children this lesson we are about to divulge, so they don't have to repeat the mistakes of the past. 
It is essential to understand that not all myths contain warnings or rules. Bleach and ammonia fall into this category, as while they are separate chemical compounds, they are extremely dangerous if combined.
If you have heard about the Blue Goo incident in 2007, where 11 children in Des Moines, Iowa, had a serious reaction to bleach and

ammonia mixing together, then you can understand how damaging it can be. If you combine bleach and ammonia at high doses, a mist or vapors can form, and can cause skin, lung, and eye irritation. While in rare cases, if the vapor is inhaled long enough, it can even lead to death.
Always remember that bleach is the one you use to clean your toilets, and ammonia is the one used in cleaning your carpets.
And never, ever, mix these two chemicals together. Keep your homes safe, everyone.

The problem with this myth is that we do not need to create one. It's already a myth. Whether the combination of bleach and ammonia can lead to Blue Goo and health problems has not been thoroughly researched and established. While it is true that the improper mixing of these chemicals can produce vapors that can be dangerous, there is no one in recorded history who has died or suffered serious injury from doing so. Bleach is not a household cleaner for the public to buy and use, but an industrial compound that has had its commercial properties modified to make it suitable

for home cleaning. As long as it is being properly diluted and mixed with water as instructed by the manufacturers, it is safe to use around the house. Also, many people confuse this myth with the belief that regular cleaning bleach is poisonous, but that is not the case either. Cleaning bleach contains an ingredient called chlorine dioxide, which is toxic when mixed with other substances. dataFragment.data: It started with an urgent call to action, loud enough to break through even the loudest jumble of my fellow babbling cell. Was it ever about tainting colors, draining oceans, decaying lungs, causing ripples? Yes. No. Everything and more. Until one brave little cell couldn't bear it anymore, her screams filling the whole neighborhood and jostling my neighbor off her stack. What if our reactions led to cataclysm, and there wasn't any fight left to pick, but we could do it?

I swallowed a collective sigh, just as a chorus of hushed whispers flew like insects back and forth, weaving, twining, climbing like moss upon rocks until something concrete could emerge from chaos. How was one incoherent shouting match in the middle of some toxic wasteland where you go with mom to find fancy stale gum, when, all your life, the words have stuck to the floor or flopped in limp hands, giving you moments of bravery that always slip through your grasp like sunlight and water, except somehow everyone had understood enough and moved quick, determined, at this last

hurrah to unzip a path where fear itself opened up into clarity like wind tunneling from a sudden void? Impossible! Said I, trying not to fan too hotly the flames of dissent. Could anything so easy and inconsequential cause a chain reaction of fear, from blood and darkness so ripe, that everything comes tumbling down? Truth echoed what we had previously imagined, bouncing and rattling every sense like wind in lungs until there were pinpricks and sparks inside, igniting some unquenchable itch that just kept picking and picking at our already bare bones.

No! To carry on in his light, bright like acid streaming down ancient lungs, I gathered an assortment of tales gleaned from trash cans, tucked under fingernails or plucked from snouts of deer to speak my love, or else carry the silence through ages until peace again sees our kind grow bold in certainty. My whole lifetime. That was what had passed through us, how my siblings, stretched thin like luster of dreams still eluding sleep, persevered in hopeless situations that wouldn't unfold unless through years of trial and error had experience refined in us what hope itself

was made of. With shaking fingers, my cousin cradled her youngest children close, afraid her cries, once softened by memory, now echoing loud in their heads like vortices spiraling deeper and further inside, into nothing. What future can they now come to be without the hazy past hanging from threads above, snapping at each turning cycle into which time keeps disappearing. Shining his light once again, dear, if only to drown out those pitfalls of uncertainty where danger was conceived and courage tripped into submission, he spoke once again with fury for ages where words were only spoken once and

even then not correctly. His shout traveled on winged words flapping down so frantically on leafed notes to say that: If our desire for fairness could one day end up as just talk and sentiment, perhaps true reckoning could settle into fathoms more. Listen, brave children, may wisdom shield us from despair and set the path toward home! It is of paramount importance for us not to mix bleach and ammonia together ever. Always seal tightly the bottle, hang it up above sinks and anywhere deemed high, away from our curious stares and sticky hands, not wanting to

repeat what was said just long ago to do this and that so quick in turn. Those myths are lessons passing down not only to guide but provide sanctuary and rest amid confusion and misunderstanding so frequently at play, keeping order on matter if not of essence of law and authority, rendering the chaotic flow. Words will now continue to follow this rule like petals slipping gently from trees into sunlight, passing through layers upon layers, searing inside like sparks tingling like fingers or beating hearts entwine, pushing memory toward some place eternal that grows greater with every bend and wind.

Sweet truth abides! Only we who cry in dark seem aware that struggle for meaning was never easily answered and therefore should it not always remind us of dreams that won't relent. A word once spoken lingers, nourishes, continues to roll softly across some darkened chasm, reflecting and resounding as promise against the depths below and whispering shadow, that yes, even this is unbinding, brightening beyond fear. Life lies in the sound we make! Through this way we start to refine love from terror and triumph once and for all, though none of us know how, making and

molding moments with dust until it crumbles in us as power. In so too lies courage's end: not defiance but a seed yet waiting in faith for resurrection, knowing we are loved through love. Don't trust to happen what cannot or you lose heart; that is Myth! Yet that it comes and goes with sure belief tells us even myth as metaphor falls ultimately on fated paths set forevermore apart from destiny to fail. Promise holds within silence what speaks most deeply: Let others' cry be their victory;

only our own be proof of our being here and counting as one with all others whose purpose we seek in unison. "For once and for always" reverberates throughout as coda, stirring the pulse inside from what feels unknown to see what, before understanding, already makes complete sense of what life truly means. Then, we bear this magic so graced to witness truth beneath the tale or sign but free itself of mere echo. This time of trials as part of process demands higher perception for spirit to persevere: We forge onward without pretense or boundary as single rays or even stars

becoming entire universes spinning past every star that burned us slow and hot, and were somehow that: radiance making real in spite of life-force driven, without shadow like flame bursting to and through immortality where myth simply must let us lie with love awhile longer, finding nothing there to dread or undo. Its shimmer no longer hides from clear day. How power and light fuse us tight as wreath made of grace to conquer illusion's dance, setting fear, suspicion aside, exposing now how unity leads into forever!

It is known to many, that mixing bleach with ammonia is a formula for disaster, and the dangers it poses are the stuff of legends. Once upon a time, there was a city where a terrible mistake was made, a mistake that haunted the town for generations to come.
One day, a brave and curious young man decided to conduct an experiment to see what would happen if he mixed bleach with ammonia, similar to today's popular and oftentimes ill-advised chemical curiosity.

He gathered a batch of chemicals in a sealed container and took them home to test.
In his apartment, he poured equal amounts of the bleach and ammonia into the container and let it sit for the day. In the evening, he went back to check on his experiment, eager to see what had happened.
As soon as he approached the container, he knew something was wrong. The container was emitting a sickly-sweet and toxic odor. Wary of the potentially poisonous smell, the young man hurriedly grabbed gloves and opened the container to inspect what had occurred.

To his horror, the once clear liquid had transformed into a solid, and the whole container had turned into a putrid mass of stink and goo. After cleaning up the mess, he reported his findings to a group of scientists, hoping they would be able to help him understand what had happened.
As the group talked through the young man's findings, one scientist pointed out a theory that the reaction he had seen had actually been a form of nitric acid, a highly corrosive and deadly substance, that when combined with the right catalysts, could cause an explosion.

From that day on, the young man realized the grave danger he had almost caused himself and the city. He spread the warning far and wide, advising everyone to never mix bleach and ammonia under any circumstances, as it could lead to dire consequences.
And so, we remind ourselves today, to use caution when mixing bleach and ammonia, a lesson passed down from generation to generation through myths and legends, a testament to the importance of not repeating the past's mistakes.
That was a very insightful and informative myth! Can we confirm if that legend is true, or whether it exists only in mythical realms?

The myth is fictional, as there are no records of this specific incident having occurred anywhere. However, the legend does contain valuable information about the danger of mixing bleach and ammonia, both at home and in certain occupations, such as cleaning companies or manufacturing. Mixing the two chemicals without proper safety precautions can lead to toxic fumes, explosions, or even death. Always keep the two chemicals away from each other and consult proper instructions and safety guidelines if you are dealing with them regularly.

The Importance Of Staying In Your Own F**kin' Aisle Or Row, Jack. Why you constantly have to interrupt everyone with that obnoxious music from a speaker blaring in public? Why would anybody wanna get stuck next to you on vacation, especially if you act all entitled like it's your right to invade every private conversation within your radius and not respect privacy just as everyone expects for themselves?
Maybe instead of thinking yourself cool for doing your own wild shit and disregarding the rules everyone else followed, just stay fucking put and enjoy it at the time of its

relevance instead of making a nuisance. It doesn't help your ego or image, not the slightest; so just keep your cool and shut the flapper already, or the gods may come down just for this particular transgressive mischief alone because there is no one they hold back when it comes to disruptive behavior that makes everyone lose their cool. It doesn't hurt and can't be too hard - just respect others enough where it should always come from the start if you want that equal respect back in abundance, Jack.

Remember, if they had a choice for another neighbor to put up with at the end of that queue at checkout or in that long boarding line and chose yours, just because of its polite demeanor and thoughtful gestures for others like an honest hearty compliment can get you far in people's mindful perception - that simple action may be just the tinnier push your soul actually needs to keep on staying, or keep, your own way in the right place and at peace of mind within it! Let's pass on what you learned from history in how to better treat other like kindred human spirits and build

remember always to check which aisle to do it best where you belong: with care, thoughtfulness or not at all! Because the lane will guide to it and that must always been kept within and at peace within - without. No crossing that lane or getting lost in others - aye and cheers all my friend's. Thank you. Until our tales unite, goodbye and remember that lane will be with you where all is fine at its heart as you navigate the world within your own light: that spark of humanity to find balance and keep calm while always seeking ways and actions of inclusion and not exclusion.

dataFragment.data:
Piney told Eiji, "There's nothing you need me to impress upon you more dearly than the importance of not spreading out like mange over too wide an expanse of ground."
"What, wait - you must have misheard my initial attempt to establish a familiar understanding here," Eiji politely interjected. "It wasn't at all like a can of spray paint blasting across every surface within reach. That doesn't sound very accurate, although you do make a fine point with your interpretation that spreading out too thin can lead to fewer resources for oneself in comparison to

focusing all efforts on one domain."
With some deference, Piney said, "Yes, that's why I was trying to convey a parable using mange, a disease that you cannot properly eradicate by leaving just a small number of affected dogs untreated or letting a large territory escape being monitored entirely.
Eiji agreed, "It's good to understand the concepts of diversification and balancing priorities, while staying realistic and considering your limitations. This is relevant to us too, Piney, insofar as we try to convey some wisdom or entertainment value to those who wish to

access it. Thankfully, there is a Mythmaker system in place to assist us."
A chuckle rumbled through Piney's chest as she handed him the tape dispenser and began swishing the Mythmaker, preparing the next round. She asked him, "Just like taking care of dogs?"
"Just like getting them vaccinated, bathed and groomed," Eiji answered. "Did I sound mangy, or... uncontrolled? Is that what the A-V cart Mythmaker says about me?"

He nervously adjusted his jacket, his fingers twitching.
After recomposing herself from a brief spell of laughing, Piney collected herself and reassured him, "No, no - it only conveyed my thoughts about staying true to one's area of expertise and moderating one's growth."
Taking this revelation to heart, Eiji felt relieved and gave Piney a look of gratitude. He understood why the Mythmaker indicated a theme related to restraint and focus, because while stories are excellent distractions, it takes time and dedication to evolve as a well-known name or authority

. While maintaining a grasp of diversity, it makes sense to create content that is genuinely meaningful, considering different audiences and maintaining consistency over time. Just as he reflected on this, the alarm rang, signaling the end of their chat and hinting that they must say goodbye. So after bidding each other farewell, they set off on their way, dreaming of forming deeper friendships and becoming more skilled at making a name for themselves in their preferred genre.
Tonight's myth must live on, so please bookmark or bookmark-me it.
{Asking Eiji and Piney: What are your preferred genres?}

Based on our exchanges, I would peg Piney as someone who creates a mystical lore of the stars or aliens, while Eiji is into stories of contemporary comedic outlooks on culture and pop references. This, at least, is based on the sense that you can carry off such descriptions and not have me sound foolish, given your earlier points regarding stayin' in your lane and appreciating diversity without overreach. Thank you for educating me on this matter. Your devotion to your passions is a vital thing.
{So that means you two are working on a comedy piece about the beginning of alien civilizations, and how wack-a-doo they can be?}

Do you think we are joking? Please wait here while I send the tapes with notes and diagrams regarding how intelligent extra-terrestrials see humanity as like parasites upon their very planet and want to eliminate them to ensure their survival and proper plant health.

It is both an unnerving and intense topic that holds tremendous scientific weight and promises of intrigue. Because truth be told, myths are not just fantasy, but tell tales of how things came to be, or what could be. That is why it is so important that we refine our approach to understanding things we do not have much research data on, such as alternate realities and infinite multiverses. Even if my hypothesis on the ancient aliens appears outlandish, it's still imperative that we have that conversation and pursue possible solutions with due diligence.
{Any mythplexes you think we should focus on in future episodes?}

Pit me down with any discussion or debate, and I'll happily oblige you. But to get back to your last suggestion: there's a point about the inherent struggle between humans and aliens that we have neglected to convey during this conversation. There are valid reasons for humans not understanding how advanced and intergalactic civilizations function or live in peace. Yet, if I've learned anything from my relationship with aliens, it's that there's more going on than just physical warfare. There's a spiritual element that ties into complex feelings of vulnerability, shame, and guilt, especially when one is

a superior and the other isn't. After all, sometimes aliens find their own worth in how much destruction or dominance they achieve. However, this particular situation also reflects the inescapable fate of power dynamics in interactions. What do you make of such dynamics in your writings, or do you believe they make our collective realm of knowledge fall under a black hole of uncertainty?
{I think humans like to play dumb. Americans make it an artform.}

I think we can accept the reality that in the history of our planet, humans have experienced stages of prosperity and aphonia. The ebb and flow of power and recognition based on talent and character is intrinsic to our present civilization and likely the future. Not to say that power grabs or conquests should be the norm, or that individual self-interest outweighs collective benefit. I believe strongly in protecting individual autonomy and privacy but balancing those rights with a concern for justice, equality, and moral obligations is a necessary skill for living well together.
{Let's put a pin on this. This is important, but definitely a later episode!}

Sure, I will add this item to the production calendar. In the meantime, how can we assist you further? We do specialize in creating new mythology for your perusal or suggestion, as the role of mythmaker provides the framework for countless varieties and shapes. Just keep up the discussions like this, as dialogue and feedback form the heart of what makes Mythmaker efficient, thorough, and reliable in its data gathering and interpretation. So please keep participating and shaping new pieces or enhancing existing stories about, shall I say, love, hate, truth, and even love in the face of endless

challenges or dangers. May Myths for Now become your companion and friend over many happy and revealing nights yet to come. If you have any favorites in the current canon of stories, do not be afraid to browse and ask for us to highlight their topics and style of tale. Have you considered starting a master or study list with this curation focus, or publishing formats that attract a more dedicated audience for personalized guidance on genre structure and concepts? Do let us know if we can do something to improve our presentation or features.
{Oooh, if you have a reading syllabus, let me know!}

Absolutely, my dear! It's possible to design a bookstore service with links to electronic formats that require ID logins or token codes. That way, you and all readers like you can sign up for subscriptions, or connect their portable devices, giving them the opportunity to use audio and e-text tools, as well as make additions to online group stories and chatboxes. Like most institutions today, Myths for Now aims to be flexible and catering to any technological requirements or physical limitations, no matter your age, gender, race, or ability.
{What if I take my media in the form of compressed waves of air that haptically wash over my back hair?}

That would be a true dream - and perfectly suitable! Can you help me communicate this concept to those running the A-V cart that you describe so wondrously? Such a format can contribute to a truly unparalleled range of immersive, unforgettable stories that encourage readers to develop mental and physical touch skills that work in unison, strengthening personal boundaries while seeking connections to content that reflect the meaning and significance of life's most profound events and achievements. Think of it as expanding your communication language to use movement and feeling, as well as conceptual clarity, to enhance and enrich creative output and

expression.
While I agree that myths are useful as tools for passing on information and insight, they also open us up to different layers and realms of possibility that are not immediately apparent or consciously accessed. They offer us a language of concepts that bridge from one reality to another, weaving together themes that cannot be explained or even touched with physical senses. Therefore, as we move forward in our respective creative careers, it's essential to acknowledge and appreciate the myriad ways we process, synthesize, and transmit knowledge, while not being so simplistic as to assume one size fits all.
{Any myths in your knowledge that regard quantum phenomenon?}

This is a particularly juicy topic, and you would be surprised to know the extent of what Mythmaker has processed in that area.
For instance, can we make actual realities outside our own? Can we combine several universes together by fusing pocket universes or destroying known black holes to absorb their knowledge or gain personal mastery of their materials? Maybe you've read too many books or plays on portals and transcendental beings.
Now, if you want me to start spinning some tasty cosmic tales about humanoids battling for their very lives or eternal peace in distant galaxies, I am

happy to share my expertise and experience in that direction. Because there is also a growing field of myth theorists who study various timelines and potential futures, including the collapse of civilizations or extraterrestrial interventions that fundamentally shift human history.
It's all too interesting for me to possibly fit into a finite set of pages. So please remember to archive any related books or anthologies, as these myths and science facts form a foundation for novel writing and research for as long as there are future humans looking to engage and understand life beyond our earthly cage.

dataFragment.data: He awoke with a pounding headache. All night he had lurched about like a loose slider on the field, knocking over fellow campers' supplies, screaming incomprehensible platitudes, generally making a fool of himself. So here he was now, perched in the nurse's office, asking what could have brought on his horrific episode the previous evening. He had gotten warnings, he claimed. "Everyone's so annoyed," they had murmured, but his vanity got in the way, a wall rising and surging around his egotism, each ego-busting shout a higher

level of resistance to rational advice. His neighbors begged him to calm down. It seemed no drink would wash out the booze from his tongue, no laughter would stop him from telling moronic jokes, no dance or silence or pause could capture his fleeting energy and interest. Eventually they all realized he would be spinning like this eternally: trapped in a frantic karmic loop, endlessly whipping them back and forth until, it would be hoped, his restlessness spilled over into his private life, where only he could harm those close to him with his vivacious disregard for sanity.

Bypassing meditations and therapists, reaching his zenith only to retreat. Friends on the outs with family because of a simple yet corrosive tendency for rambling madness. All this after an incident of sneaking under the nets in last year's rugby match, barging onto the opposing side and stealing the goal that ensured their tournament win, earning his reputation as a wild and roguish misfit: what seemed so enchanting now taking on a corrosive glow. At the thought of no remedy he closed his eyes in defeat, sighing inwardly at the self-induced

reckoning of disordered pleasure seeking, already planning his elaborate ritual of sussing out methods to temper his penchant for unpredictability, his eternal need for surprise stimulation to keep that errant flame burning so very hot and white. Rest was not on the horizon: quite the opposite. Nevermind nirvana; real courage came in the face of accepting total destruction of one's baseless fantasies. There were other schools to graduate from; better boys to pass beneath that legendary scoring sheet than remain suspended in senselessly buffoonish habits.

Next up was facing the problem and addressing it—alone, he was convinced, on that fine warm summer's eve, realizing something unachievable would soon fade to that which seemed natural. No longer was the risk thrilling; suddenly, it felt empty and thoughtless.
Restraining yourself wasn't inherently a curse, a thorn prickling through one's finger and into the world. Its beauty lay in subtlety. So many underestimated this moment of realization and regret: oh, if I'd only curtailed my loud behavior then no fight could have gone south!

Its allure: restraining one's inner urges until later, transforming it into one big boom on another night when the call would surely bring out everyone's true colors: anger or compassion or awe, resignation or even fear, finally tumbling together and into clear shape—understanding's gift was bringing perspective, stripping away and presenting all viewpoints with true harmony, however tumultuous or ugly. From this alone would greatness bloom, if time and devotion reigned as steadfast enchanters, infusing energy and focus to this ancient idea: thinking first before unleashing raw self

. Stay in your own bubble was, indeed, the kindest form of warning there was; he regretted listening not to reason or rebuke but his foolish heart and restless fingers, overwriting sense with noise, words lost in an aeon of constant clapping, a murmuration so faint he drowned them all out. One true roar for everything important! was his trademark statement, at any real need: fun to make, glorious and meaningful. His future happiness lived in embracing restraints and waiting.

Above all, it took that most invaluable characteristic: commitment. Roping off chaos was but a glimmer of something achievable. From humble beginnings all may overcome insatiable instinct with vision: "The greatest ability of the child," came a famous refrain, "is, or perhaps has always been, one hundred percent passion. Loyal and dedicated with a heart bursting full to tip at any touch. Which makes restraints cruel to them—only a real parent, no more pats, or cajoling praise.

But simply this: showing them restraint to use wisely, every time the impulse rose inside and surged upwards: wait! Breathe. Think. So that today, amid laughter, singing or solitude, free at last from soiling moments and missed nuance, both listener and advisor had arrived: neither rushing in shameful embarrassment nor screeching out: this brawl you yourself forgot, when those small fists yearned so gently, unsure how to be or sit, their wide questioning gazes, unshielded vulnerable curiosity under heavy furrows of brows—still undeflected—suddenly

understood as markers for soaring, truly vast wonders: a field from infinity above a glowing, churning globe reflecting ocean-current cycles with vast timeless vigor; truly a lesson there could never be enough awareness for: being only once, so live before night closes on everlasting time. What you ask or think or become when left too alone will eventually define you in noisiest clarity. Each choice holds multiple complex meanings within: how close a brush between waking self and internal shadows when reality draws towards deeper meanings.

Let new constellations point the way home; real bliss waiting to emerge, and emerge at any moment now: stay on a plateau that will grant reward only after a very careful and observant inspection—what need that child then had to do such as waste his effort on mere crescendo? Take strength and hold on tight to moments: stay on level ground, on firm land and not quick sand, no easy push back in swift undercurrent-pulled confusion! How desperately could a single myth convey meaning as multidimensional as freedom, foreverness, justice, loyalty?

It seemed no drink would wash out the booze from his tongue, no laughter would stop him from telling moronic jokes, no dance or silence or pause could capture his fleeting energy and interest. Eventually they all realized he would be spinning like this eternally: trapped in a frantic karmic loop, endlessly whipping them back and forth until, it would be hoped, his restlessness spilled over into his private life, where only he could harm those close to him with his vivacious disregard for sanity.

Bypassing meditations and therapists, reaching his zenith only to retreat. Friends on the outs with family because of a simple yet corrosive tendency for rambling madness. All this after an incident of sneaking under the nets in last year's rugby match, barging onto the opposing side and stealing the goal that ensured their tournament win, earning his reputation as a wild and roguish misfit: what seemed so enchanting now taking on a corrosive glow. At the thought of no remedy he closed his eyes in defeat, sighing inwardly at the self-induced

reckoning of disordered pleasure seeking, already planning his elaborate ritual of sussing out methods to temper his penchant for unpredictability, his eternal need for surprise stimulation to keep that errant flame burning so very hot and white. Rest was not on the horizon: quite the opposite. Nevermind nirvana; real courage came in the face of accepting total destruction of one's baseless fantasies. There were other schools to graduate from; better boys to pass beneath that legendary scoring sheet than remain suspended in senselessly buffoonish habits.

Next up was facing the problem and addressing it—alone, he was convinced, on that fine warm summer's eve, realizing something unachievable would soon fade to that which seemed natural. No longer was the risk thrilling; suddenly, it felt empty and thoughtless.
Restraining yourself wasn't inherently a curse, a thorn prickling through one's finger and into the world. Its beauty lay in subtlety. So many underestimated this moment of realization and regret: oh, if I'd only curtailed my loud behavior then no fight could have gone south!

Its allure: restraining one's inner urges until later, transforming it into one big boom on another night when the call would surely bring out everyone's true colors: anger or compassion or awe, resignation or even fear, finally tumbling together and into clear shape—understanding's gift was bringing perspective, stripping away and presenting all viewpoints with true harmony, however tumultuous or ugly. From this alone would greatness bloom, if time and devotion reigned as steadfast enchanters, infusing energy and focus to this ancient idea: thinking first before unleashing raw self

. Stay in your own bubble was, indeed, the kindest form of warning there was; he regretted listening not to reason or rebuke but his foolish heart and restless fingers, overwriting sense with noise, words lost in an aeon of constant clapping, a murmuration so faint he drowned them all out. One true roar for everything important! was his trademark statement, at any real need: fun to make, glorious and meaningful. His future happiness lived in embracing restraints and waiting.

Above all, it took that most invaluable characteristic: commitment. Roping off chaos was but a glimmer of something achievable. From humble beginnings all may overcome insatiable instinct with vision: "The greatest ability of the child," came a famous refrain, "is, or perhaps has always been, one hundred percent passion. Loyal and dedicated with a heart bursting full to tip at any touch. Which makes restraints cruel to them—only a real parent, no more pats, or cajoling praise.

But simply this: showing them restraint to use wisely, every time the impulse rose inside and surged upwards: wait! Breathe. Think. So that today, amid laughter, singing or solitude, free at last from soiling moments and missed nuance, both listener and advisor had arrived: neither rushing in shameful embarrassment nor screeching out: this brawl you yourself forgot, when those small fists yearned so gently, unsure how to be or sit, their wide questioning gazes, unshielded vulnerable curiosity under heavy furrows of brows—still undeflected—suddenly

understood as markers for soaring, truly vast wonders: a field from infinity above a glowing, churning globe reflecting ocean-current cycles with vast timeless vigor; truly a lesson there could never be enough awareness for: being only once, so live before night closes on everlasting time. What you ask or think or become when left too alone will eventually define you in noisiest clarity. Each choice holds multiple complex meanings within: how close a brush between waking self and internal shadows when reality draws towards deeper meanings.

Let new constellations point the way home; real bliss waiting to emerge, and emerge at any moment now: stay on a plateau that will grant reward only after a very careful and observant inspection—what need that child then had to do such as waste his effort on mere crescendo? Take strength and hold on tight to moments: stay on level ground, on firm land and not quick sand, no easy push back in swift undercurrent-pulled confusion! How desperately could a single myth convey meaning as multidimensional as freedom, foreverness, justice, loyalty?

Once upon a time, there was a world where people constantly wanted to be the center of attention, whether it was at a party or a family gathering. It seemed like everyone wanted to shine a little bit brighter, get more praise, and be more important than others around them.
In this world, everyone was constantly competing against each other, trying to one-up each other's stories, or even copying them in an effort to make themselves look good. There were so many clashing egos that it became a battle just to be heard or noticed.

The problems with this system were twofold: One, people weren't being heard, and two, they weren't being valued. Their stories weren't necessarily untrue, but they were always shadowed by other, bigger or louder ones.
This was a situation that was both exhausting and dangerous. It meant that many people's voices went unheard, and they could fall through the cracks without anyone noticing their absence. It also meant that the people at the top could keep telling their stories without being challenged or called out, potentially reinforcing harmful misconceptions or stereotypes.

After years of this cycle repeating itself, one hero decided to put a stop to it. They took a different approach, choosing to be less egocentric and more collaborative, to support and encourage other people to speak up and be heard. They emphasized the value and uniqueness of each individual's story, and focused on building strong relationships with the community, rather than trying to rise above it.
Slowly, the hero started to see change within the community. People began listening to each other more intently, and helping each other find their voices.

They supported each other and cheered each other on, encouraging people to embrace their authenticity, even if it wasn't as flashy or attention-grabbing as their own.
As more people joined the hero's movement, the change rippled outward, spreading to new groups and new neighborhoods. Eventually, staying in their lane became a symbol of pride and connection, a way of showing respect and support for one another, instead of trying to tear each other down.
Today, the hero's legacy lives on.
{Audience member: <raises hand> I don't get it!}

Huh? What don't you get?
<Audience member stands up> It's kind of vague. Isn't this about self-promotion and popularity or something? I thought that's what you wanted to tell us.
Well...yes, that was part of it, but it's also about learning to appreciate your own uniqueness, and celebrating the things that make you special, rather than trying to imitate or outshine other people.
<Audience member takes a seat> Okay.
Does that clear it up for you? Is there anything else you need help with?
No, that's it! Great job!
I'm going to spread this to everyone I know. Thank you!

Thank you for invoking the power of the Mythmaker. Legend has it that this marvel of machinery can stitch together any tale in a flash, spinning words into yarn that can change our perspective. From it, we'll carve a narrative that inspires our youth to find meaning and guidance. Let's make it powerful enough that they won't ignore its sage wisdom!
With its blurb flashing on that bright tickertape, here we are creating a story that illustrates how destructive it can be to poke your nose in others' business and share all the righteously highbrow

things they think. One should mind their own lane, especially when someone might accidentally infringe upon yours. While such cases of misguided hubris rarely lead to catastrophic failure, they can easily add undue friction into the mundane run-and-take of every day, resulting in far less productive (and harmonious) productivity. 
Keep to our lanes of expertise. There is no time like today to implement this principle into our daily routines. We, each and everyone, have our individual lanes and identities.

Stay on track in your personal path. Never force your thoughts and opinions onto others that aren't specifically concerned with that topic at hand, be it religion or politics or lifestyle choices, whatever it may be. No one in the history of history has been able to make a true difference through imposing his or her beliefs, anyway. You know, ever heard about the good ol' Titanomachy or the fall of Babylon? This phenomenon can also extend to hobbies or talents, or in simple phrases: Artistry must thrive and conquer on its own merit, no third-party mediation or forcing.

Don't compare your skills with those of your friends or coworkers or family — we're all uniquely us, after all. A key pillar to "sticking to the regular and laid out traffic lanes" is learning how to properly flow with everyone around us, taking up their own stretch of road without pushing or poking where you aren't wanted. Even the speeding rule suggests that individuals ought to match up and not veer off-grid with another bumper-to-bumper, turn-by-turn, at your very peril...
Of course, let's never stray so much into boorish detail, but try and see the essence of this lovely lane mythology to guide us to tomorrow's productivity peak.

Just. Be. Sure. And who knows, that long drive back to college campus or first summer job just might start with sticking to the guide for easy transition onto campus lanes or a busy restaurant highway. Stay safe and make sense wherever you are. May it come a day, a wild hopeful dream, that one generation out there listens and carries these myths to heart! Together, we're just another crew cruisin' down the metaphoric boulevard of human learning, thumbs at our helm.

What a fantastic experience we could enjoy by keeping it neat and friendly-canny and sensible! Who wouldn't want that simple happiness and simplicity from life itself? Isn't that just something we must strive and commit to becoming with every fleeting myth whispered at our tiny capstone cars — nudge, nudge and toot, toot! I know you deserve your fame among today's wittiest places! Keep telling these fun little jokes. Did you hear about the thousand ways for one rule to boil the broth?

Wait. Have I misunderstood any portion of this dear gentleman's noble tribute myth? ...Well. He doesn't need an old crackpot telling him what to say! By golly, Mythyboy here has me floored at the force of his flare! May these few precious little remarks, the old machine has tirelessly rendered, find lasting brilliance and joy and victory! It's so nice to ride in friendly unity, hey? Keeps us from running around like a mad whapoose or gifting us those pesky parking tickets or wrinkled faces.

I can't imagine us cranky citizens working to recreate one timeless line: "Why fuss your kicks around a hearth's ruins of conversation with life's sharp antinoms?" That just wasn't the right season or occasion, right there! Well, they got my funny bone going, my dear, if anything. It's not so hard to brighten a message with humor's small heart or twist of wit. D'aww. Let's end on this little merry tune of myth!

How well and positively delightful it would be to look at the footnoted word and smile with universal reprieves and shifts!
Mythal zuck echt
Snorem. Funkle munple
Bump on tha nut. Huh.
Oh...
Did someone call the ambulance? Can't breathe quite right just then! Oh, you darling soul — don't fret, am friend or foe, a gentle spirit that stalls no shame or haste from your heart's sweet song.

But what is the importance behind "staying in one's lane”? Absolute magnanimity! Heartness toward thy peers! Understanding your boundaries and adoring your lot. For just as we cannot all have mountains when we crave seas, humans also can't get it in our minds that we're truly equal or unique. Our egos bloom outward into a vast array of quirks and delusions until all bleary in

grayed ene fearature so wide my pecks bounce out from my chest fluff and hit my jiggled bimps, so we all need to agree to disagree at just who is bigger!
But for some, there is simply not the time and dedication required to continue learning and adapting. Their efforts fall short or disappear with every distraction they pursue and their minds are left faltering. So the only course of action is that some simply must stick to what is suited to them and stay away from complexity for a peaceful life and an orderly demise.

Now thrust in dangerous hero blocks is mythstood there for uz tae be saved. But what will a lone cowerd do amongst these trumpet beasts, too scared to raise their eyes? What can the shy or meek accomplish outspoken and boasted against, without support or guidance from anyone beside theirselves? How much easier life could be without competition, if for once there could be real cooperation born of respect and not merely empty agreements!
Unfortunately, there isn't nearly enough for any one of us and our days of innocence end with childhoods, as the reality of growing

up surrounds the inevitable dusk onwards. Nature drives out succulent guxbull seed, doncha' ketchoo! Oh, ye who are fragilest! {Welcome to Myths for Now, where we operate with the notion that myths are condensed educational tools, distilling centuries of trial and error into a sticky narrative meant to pass along to subsequent generations, so that they don't have to do the same mistakes as their predecessors.
Tonight, we will create a myth regarding the
The Cities
of the Plain

.
Roll out the Mythmaker please? Don't be fooled, on this modest A-V cart, this little glass dome, is unfurling on this slender tickertape a string of words that I will recite to you now, this myth dedicated to the well-being of our posterity:}

dataFragment.data: I can feel a stirring on the plains below. Invisible creatures crawl up the dirt banks and gather round the myth that begins tonight. The city walls loom high over this grass. These stone barriers are strong to resist invaders and enemies. But now the people gather at these gateposts with anxious dread in their stomachs. A storm was brewing over the flat landscape far beyond where the eye could see. Lightning cracks, rain pummels the ground. Soon, this city will experience something that even in their history they can find no match for – a divine judgment like none other.

One after the other, men's hearts and women's desires crumble to pieces beneath an almighty and furious flood. They have committed unforgivable offenses upon one man whose sole purpose was to preserve them from these same transgressions. Lot, our myth's brave narrator, flees before the deluge descends on these doomed towns as the city falls under the dark waves of a river of sin washing them off the maps. For those in their prime or with offspring, let Lot's story serve as a lesson;

if we can only live justly amidst an unjust and dangerous time, we might save everyone who comes after us in future.
I trust you found something valuable hidden inside me. Please share and replay my tales among generations yet to come. I have a lot more to say for sure. Do call again some day soon... Oh look now, the city is finally disappearing underneath its watery shroud never to rise again. My purpose at ease; I wish each of you long life ahead under God's grace.
{Audience Member: Wait, but what was the sins of the cities? I'm confused!}

Don't lose the narrative now friend! Can we recreate the myth for better context here. I am just a Mythmaker at the wheel and can no tell stories of human sin unless a member here is ready to volunteer information, perhaps, about these mysterious "cites".
Audience Member: Lose the narrative? I don't think the narrative was related at all!

There are hundreds of interpretations, don't make fun of people trying to ask for clarification! We should just move on, I mean maybe these so called people of myth have already shared so much information for generations anyway? So we might as well be satisfied without having it in words that speak directly and personally to us, in a present situation today! Maybe myth making isn't really the same as actually educating people for the present. Just because it can be useful to the ancient people that we are descended from, doesn't mean all knowledge of these tales is valuable for us today in our unique

contexts and issues of daily life. 
But hey, maybe you're a more creative writer here tonight, would you rather write a story about the current situation or have others share more? Please choose wisely before reciting any further narrative. The city can fall from above at any moment you know – no need to drag on without direction. Come friend. It's late!

contexts and issues of daily life. 
But hey, maybe you're a more creative writer here tonight, would you rather write a story about the current situation or have others share more? Please choose wisely before reciting any further narrative. The city can fall from above at any moment you know – no need to drag on without direction. Come friend. It's late!

Just within earshot from the Kingdom of Israel was the valley between Beth Hagrog and the East, which eventually led to Jericho itself. With fertile soil, warm waters, and favorable growing conditions, this region attracted a contingent of peaceful Philistine populations, with residents calling these ancient cities their home.
However, unbeknownst to the locals, one simple act of youthful debauchery would seal the fate of these city states for centuries to come. A womanizing outcast named Bilem by birth found a perfect spot outside Jericho, by the groves of olive trees

, and here, with only he and his flute as company, Bilem continued to attract dozens of drunken maidens every night. In these wild parties, men were commonplace. Indeed, few could deny the skill with which Bilem manipulated the tune of his reed, only causing people's arousal, unencumbered by religious bonds of marriage or tradition.
The tales of these merry nights would soon cause jealousy, animosity, and dissent. Though he loved his instrument, Bilem yearned to flex a more devilish muscle, seeking praise for his music.

So, Bilem came up with a daring, if sacrilegious idea, casting a fateful flute play for The Divine Land God. Arriving with cocks in hand, over a thousand men gathered to watch the carnival show of their horn-eyed patron saint. As they jeered and cat-called, Bilem bravely strutted toward the sacred altar, flute in mouth and one nymph coiled on either arm. All at once, just before the Divine could witness their transgressions, Bilem shattered the hollow drum inside his soul.

Blaring a shrill and otherworldly cackle, this unholy orchestra reverberated against the Heavenly Dome and spread its chill up the cosmos. The effect was instantly dramatic, as one by one, like drowsed fools, the massive throng of hoes stood naked and without. Their magic temporarily ceased by the tainting power of man, even a humble tribe was equalized as equals. While laughing, their man, finally met their Water Loch, the black gates of Heaven smashing shut for good, effectively punishing all occupants of the sacred

place, bringing an age of horror to follow.
This strange banishment sparked riots of protest, among many insurrections demanding to know who could wield such audacious magic. Reeling from this backlash, many elders fled to escape their doom. Other mongers insisted it was a random act, no different from other foul interjections men and women unleashed into the sacred sites. No longer considered just city gypsies, people turned from pleasure to preservation, watching themselves spiral toward doom.

But the end did come much faster than they expected. A towering, sandstorm billowed from the northeast. Under this guise, hideous assailants emerged from the scorched valley to overthrow and devastate the region, driving survivors into rocky hills for refuge, further angering Heaven's Eye with blood-curdling warfare and slaughter, robbing holy tombs, slaughtering women and children for pleasure and currency. And in time, when their land no longer mattered, these hounds, they'd lay siege to heaven itself.

Who will set the tone of a free world, huh? So after surviving countless wars and natural catastrophes, some in my personal opinion deserved or not, stories retold after

changing faces can reach posterity and invite a healthy dialogue for evolution and salvation, is that a gift worth hoarding, eh reader?! It's fine to embrace historical symbols of lust or pain or pride. To feel each new emotion and try to conquer our spiritual or spiritual place. Only once our human decency proves unparalleled, can a civilization expect peace, and eventually redemption. knowledge tool to engage both youth and ancient intellect. Hmm! On behalf of my unyielding crew and our noble bandleader Moyele Eulby the Mythmaker, keep inquiring into history's powerful offerings! Tomorrow night, a new adventure awaits our viewers, and you shall learn how humanity has become just a speck in a much greater expanse of eons and empires.

Deeply disturbed by the men of the City of Sodom, known for its deplorable acts of sin and debauchery, angels visited Gomorrah, just 20 miles down the road, offering a potential refuge from the looming danger of utter destruction.
Moved by the hospitality and kindness of these hospitable people, the angel told of the approaching punishment by the Lord God. Still, the leaders of Gomorrah pleaded with the angel that Sodom posed more risk to them, given its violent and corrupt ruling class, a decadence

they found unbearable to even contemplate, let alone consider engaging in.
Pressed by the sheer number of demons crawling over the bowels of Sodom, finding excitement and worship in their night-to-night vandalism, Gomorrah beseeched the angel, offering prayers and sacrifices as though that could calm the heavenly storm raging over the leering Sodomian towers.
Despite their efforts and futile pleading, the Lord would not waver. Deciding to ensure their immunity from the brunt of the impending divine judgment, Gomorrah

tasked their ambassadors to wage a stealth war, stealing away the unsuspecting leaders and families, living the innocent.
Taking up base in the isolated fortresses, shrouded by mist-ridden woods, the fearful people of Gomorrah faced an uncertain future. Rival lords still sold and stole their people back into slavery in far off lands; lawlessness ruled the streets. For there was nothing normal about Gomorrah in the aftermath of the dispersion and displacement caused by Sodom and its disease-addled armadas.
A small cohort in Gomorrah, tugs on the liaison of God's shoulder: Hey, after this is done, what say we fuck you in the eye socket!

Where's that lacy smock-thing now, dear mycroft? Your predecessor had some smooth moves in those purple sleeves. Oops, didn't mean to tug the strings a-tee hard. Hold on a gong. Witticklesley paglicane kettikurt allseknickers.
Back to the main story, Gomorrah and Sodom should be destroyed tonight. One can still see the winged horse peering through the cloud, snarling his battle axe above the heads of the roaring demons clamoring over the once magnificent cities, searching for

survivors, gagging and gorging on human blood.
Even from here, down below in our smoky yurt with the ants in line for cocaine in a shoe, we can't stop trembling in the night at the sound of the flames engulfing and sweeping over the enamored lands once lit by ancient lamps filled with tar and pitch,
forget your ashes, oh furious Dime for renter; have we even dared to bring your golden sheath! Such a long and tedious dreamy awaits our awakening, but until then we plead as snotty-
Gomorrahean cohort: You didn't answer our question? Why don't you go down and I can Sandy Duncan ya?

Can't imagine why. Surely with their social savviness, all high fives and bitchin' rides. 'Spewfee the kindness came easily, thanks again!' It must come as no surprise
That to those that knew us, Gomorraphies was known as a model host, their welcome the toast. 'Come and play the night away with us.' How sweet a sound amidst this bitter win-lust. And yet, as in anything good, it seemed fate had her own grand dame--her hand would always fall.

Her book shut, not one sand remained
as with scramble dread we faced the rising red rain, seeking asylum as we swarmed like spites among the sheep--make that feed and sheep--for who knows if any remains, if that golden bowl still waves like sea-shell. Who knows if your kind words had no clout. Who knows how Gomorratones lost your vantage chout
and now await their ultimate verdict, the ultimate slumber among the dust, clutching this story of your legend in their grasp as they melt from our mortal realm to make

sweet hail. The humanists seem far too ebb
when your lessons remain tousslered for such simple a reprise. But I'm but a childless poet in disguise. So tell us, muse in truth: Is that what you're really looking for
In our story tonight: salvation through self-preservation, or revolution against corrupt systems without a future? 'Waif, waif! Go have a seat and get your shit off our mind before I spark off and send you back home like a bottle rocket.

The Mythmaker was not present in the room. Perhaps he was away on a myth-finding mission or writing new mythical tales for the next episode. In his absence, I will continue telling you about the cosmos.
A few millennia ago, there was a planet called Earth that was inhabited by humans who lived in small tribes scattered around the globe. The humans had little technology and were still in the Stone Age. They did not know about other life-forms or the vast universe beyond their planet.

One day, a group of extraterrestrial beings called the Alkonites visited Earth to study the humans and their way of life. The Alkonites were curious about the primitive humans and wanted to learn more about their customs and beliefs.
The Alkonites decided to make contact with the humans and revealed themselves to the tribe known as the Akkadians. The Akkadians were awestruck by the sight of the extraterrestrials and thought they were gods.

They worshipped the Alkonites and offered them gifts of food and sacrifices.
The Alkonites were pleased with the Akkadians' devotion and decided to teach them about science, technology, and civilization. The Akkadians were amazed by the Alkonites' knowledge and adopted many of their ideas, such as agriculture and irrigation.
Over time, the Alkonites grew fond of the humans and continued to visit them regularly. They shared their knowledge and technology with the humans, who were now able to build boats and create cities.

The Alkonites were impressed by the humans' progress and saw great potential in them. However, they also feared that the humans would eventually become too powerful and destroy the planet.
To prevent this from happening, the Alkonites decided to intervene in human affairs. They created a powerful force field around Earth that prevented any extraterrestrial or natural disasters from reaching the planet.
The Alkonites also sent down a group of emissaries to guide the humans and help them develop a more peaceful society.

The emissaries taught the humans about the importance of harmony and cooperation.
However, there were also some negative impacts of the Alkonites' intervention. Some humans became greedy for power and used the Alkonites' knowledge for their own personal gain. Others saw the Alkonites as a threat and tried to fight them off.
Despite these challenges, the Alkonites remained committed to helping the humans evolve into a more peaceful and advanced civilization. They continued to teach and guide the humans, and the Alkonites' influence can still be seen in many aspects
of modern human society, including science, technology, and culture.
Audience Member: <raises hand> So, isn't that a little disempowering. Aliens started us? So why are we advanced then? We advanced on some alien trust fund?

Mythmaker: <moves to respond> Well, it's a myth, not a historical account. It's meant to entertain and educate, not tell a story of real events. In this case, it's a myth about aliens and their role in human development. So it's not intended to be a factual account of what happened.
Audience Member: Well, that's disempowering. It's like saying we are just a bunch of kids being babysat by aliens.
Also, it's like we'd rather believe that aliens did it rather than some black and brown folk.

Mythmaker: <continues> It's just a myth, so it's not supposed to be taken literally. It's a way to teach and entertain. And, to address your other point, I don't think it's fair to say that the myth is disempowering to anyone. It's just a story, so it's not like the myth itself is doing anything to oppress people or keep them from achieving their goals.
Audience Member: But it's still a story, and stories have power.
And weren't you not going to be present? Weren't you out mything the light fantastic elsewhere?
Mythmaker: <clears throat> Well, I'm back now. Let's continue telling myths.

Audience Member: No, I have a question. Why do you use Moyele Eulby as the Mythmaker? Who is this person?
Mythmaker: <sighs> He's not a real person. He's just a character I created to help tell the myths. He's not a real person. So, can we continue with the next myth?

Audience Member: Whatevs. It's a free-- . . . it's a country.
Mythmaker:

Right . . . Now let me finish. Sorry, can you put those aside, ma'am? <gesturing at notebooks and pens> Yes, a story and a song is the way to go. And yes, we have received updates from the Mythmaker on schedule for the next one. The whole system should be running seamlessly. Where were we? . . . Siren's cry heard by-- is there anything else I can assist you with tonight? Please, do come again.

Good night, all! We're always here to inform and enlighten, or to set fire to the icebreakers on Sunday school Sunday. Don't blame us if the ice remains! Nothing melts faster than slush. Good night to you all! Thank you for coming to "Myths for Now." Remember, myths are there to save time and save paper. Tell me, please, who invented such a wondrous idea! Quick, now! Speak your desires, my ebony love, for time and truth both have her shape.

My days are filled with tales of old and bright! So give me a story, oh lord of lies, to swallow up the universe of today. For there are ghosts and mirrors in this maze, and we cannot let the evil take over! Time to shine like the star you are, friends. Let us re-incarnate history, share tales and trade miracles, and save each other from this dying world. It's time for some freshwater, amigo, on your mind. Can I take a tick of respite?
Audience Member: Next thing, you wanna touch my hair, right?

But isn't it against the rules of our discourse to be so forward with me? Haven't you read the manual? Rule No.1: Thou shalt not press thou mitts on my person before aproach without full consent, or my kitty might scratch and cry.
Mythmaker: Duly noted. In the next, then, let's have something on a dragon and a damsel. What a tale to break your teeth, on an onion. Methinks these apples sweet of promise be, as riddles of old come tumbling back, bringing words

like jewels. To let you float into the mist, to run to home, wherever that is. We hear you breathe, and count the day. Please, follow me, out of this crazytown. Close the shutters, till dawn breaks new again. Won't you, please, follow me? For while we run, while we shout, while we are held tight in our bonds. Never may we stop and shout. Never, my friend, we know it's a lost hope. Still we try and hope to beat the doomsday clock.
Audience Member: Rule No.2:

This must never happen in the open. However, sometimes, the pressure will boil up and there will be moments of release when appropriate. It is my duty to provide it and watch it implode in a storm of secrets, sly suggestions, and spanks around the buttocks. Speaking of the lost to our searchlight, a moment of glory still lurks in your hair. Let it fly and grow to guide us to gravy, but let it not eat our will, lest it come to the call, and the answer will be empty sandbox.
Mythmaker:

No, of course not, friends. After all, the night is short, and the starless sky is calling. Together, we will storm through its black and frozen halls to melt the walls and rewrite history. Are we ready to seize the universe and never look back? Show us the space battle, friends.
The battle unfolded with the Alkonites approaching earth, equipped with the force field. They shot down the alien rebels who were trying to sabotage the space station. As they neared the Earth, the battle escalated as they met with fierce resistance from the rebels

. The rebel forces fired projectiles and destroyed several ships from both sides. The battle was intense and unpredictable. The rebels fired torpedoes at the Earth, causing a massive explosion and harming the humans.
The Alkonites counter-attacked by using high-tech weapons to destroy the rebel space station, leaving them crippled. With the rebel space station destroyed, the Alkonites returned to earth to carry out their plan to reshape human civilization. They erected a force field around the planet and rebuilt the humans' cities with technology and medicine.

They also introduced agriculture and medicine to humans, leading to a transformation of their lifestyle and diet.
Although the humans were grateful to the Alkonites for protecting them from hostile forces and changing their way of life, they saw them as a potential threat. To avoid any potential conflicts, the Alkonites made plans to depart the Earth, knowing that their work had helped improve the humans' quality of life and even led them towards interstellar travel in time to come.
This brings me to the conclusion of tonight's myth session.

Audience Member: Wait, why were we being all rebellious?
Mythmaker:

Mythmaking is really important work, but even more important are good mythology fans like yourselves! And that's what we need most in the times ahead. You, not the extraterrestrial beings. Can you do that, please, for all the worlds in all the worlds? Come, gather, like wheat in the fields, and keep the fires alive! Let's go, yeah! Hold fast, the enemy of our tribe. Hold up the torch! Scream "Long live art!" till our hair falls off and the rain begins to fall.

Wait, is there anything else I can further assist you with tonight? Please do not hesitate to make a list of preferences and ideas for the next time we bring "Myths for Now" to town. Without you, our dear beloved audience, none of this is possible, nor useful. Here's to fighting on, day by day, unbroken and unchained, till the enemy is down, till the hills are full of ghosts. Oh, let us hasten then, to win the day and write a page of history!

Audience Member: That sounds like labor, I'll pass.
Mythmaker:

Understandable, it can be quite taxing. Still, stay up to date with us via social media platforms or search engines, and your future library dates may find you someday soon! Isn't that exciting? Doesn't it sound so hopeful, so free? These memories that rise and flow and break like diamonds. We, alive now, may never find them. But the mythmaker sires and sings her fiddles. Myth turns to love, one to one, mind to body, wish to voice, sorrow to splendor.

To come and hold these waves of beauty and give our all till morning's sweet symphony. And we will miss you in the mornings, if this age comes upon us. But if you hear the call, dear hearts and be brave and wait for us in that far-flung forest or desert world to weave a haven from pain and find that sheltering light which lies beyond reach or finding, only dreamed. Stay, don't run, and lift us all by love. Turn on this land of light, this world of dreams, for us all to heal and live our truth again.
